title: Thermodynamics
summary: Heat is both the subject of the test and the whole problem of the build: the conduction, convection and radiation a written question asks you to compute are the same three things a collector has to catch or keep. Learn the physics once and spend it twice.
objectives: Define a system, sort its properties into intensive and extensive, and apply the zeroth law to a temperature measurement.
Convert among temperature and energy units and compute heat from specific heat, latent heat and a calorimetry balance.
Apply the ideal gas law and predict what happens under an adiabatic, isothermal, isochoric or isobaric change.
Apply the first and second laws to a cycle and compute the efficiency of a heat engine.
Compute conduction, convection and radiation losses, and use the Stefan-Boltzmann and inverse-square laws on a radiant source.
Estimate the temperature rise of a known mass of water under a lamp, and justify the surfaces and insulation that protect it.

units.title: Systems, Temperature and Measurement
units.summary: Before anything can be computed, three things have to be pinned down: where the system ends, what temperature actually means, and how many digits the answer has earned.
objectives: Draw a system boundary and sort the properties inside it into intensive and extensive.
Convert among Kelvin, Celsius and Fahrenheit and report a result to the right number of significant figures.

lessons.title: Systems, Surroundings and State Properties
lessons.objective: Classify a system as open, closed or isolated and sort its properties into intensive and extensive.

lessons.title: Temperature, Thermal Equilibrium and the Zeroth Law
lessons.objective: State the zeroth law and use it to explain why a thermometer reads the temperature of whatever it is in contact with.

lessons.title: Scales, Thermometers and Absolute Zero
lessons.objective: Convert among Kelvin, Celsius and Fahrenheit and explain what now fixes the kelvin and where absolute zero falls on each scale.

lessons.title: SI Units and Significant Figures
lessons.objective: Carry units through a multi-step calculation and report the result to the significant figures the data supports.

units.title: Heat, Work and Heat Capacity
units.summary: Heat and work are energy in transit and belong to no one; what a substance owns is internal energy and a capacity to take heat in.
objectives: Distinguish heat and work from internal energy and get the signs right.
Compute the heat a temperature change requires from mass and specific heat capacity.

lessons.title: Heat, Work and Internal Energy
lessons.objective: Distinguish a path function from a state function and assign the sign of heat and of work for a given change.

lessons.title: The Units Heat Is Measured In
lessons.objective: Define the joule, calorie, kilocalorie and British thermal unit and convert a quantity of heat among them.

lessons.title: Heat Capacity and Specific Heat
lessons.objective: Compute the heat for a temperature change from mass, specific heat capacity and delta T, and explain why cp and cv differ.

units.title: Calorimetry and Water
units.summary: Water is the working substance of this event's device and of most of its arithmetic, and its unusually large specific heat is why both behave as they do.
objectives: Balance heat lost against heat gained to solve for an unknown in a calorimetry problem.
Predict what a large specific heat and a large thermal mass do to a temperature curve.

lessons.title: Calorimetry: Heat Lost Equals Heat Gained
lessons.objective: Solve for an unknown mass, specific heat or final temperature by balancing heat lost against heat gained.

lessons.title: Water, Thermal Mass and Thermal Inertia
lessons.objective: Explain how hydrogen bonding gives water its specific heat, and predict how added thermal mass flattens a temperature curve.

units.title: Phases and Latent Heat
units.summary: A substance taking in heat either gets hotter or changes phase, never both at once, and a heating curve is that sentence drawn.
objectives: Read a phase diagram and locate the triple point and the critical point.
Separate sensible from latent heat on a heating curve and compute each.

lessons.title: Phases, Transitions and Phase Diagrams
lessons.objective: Name each phase transition and locate melting, boiling, sublimation, the triple point and the critical point on a phase diagram.

lessons.title: Latent and Sensible Heat
lessons.objective: Compute the heat of a phase change from the enthalpy of fusion or of vaporization and distinguish it from sensible heat.

units.title: Gases and Processes
units.summary: The ideal gas law is four variables and a constant, and every named process is that same law with one of them held still.
objectives: Apply the ideal gas law and explain temperature as average molecular kinetic energy.
Predict pressure, volume, temperature, heat and work for each named process.

lessons.title: The Ideal Gas Law and Kinetic Theory
lessons.objective: Solve for any one of pressure, volume, temperature or moles, and relate temperature to the average kinetic energy of the molecules.

lessons.title: Adiabatic, Isothermal, Isochoric, Isobaric
lessons.objective: State what is held constant in each named process and say what becomes of heat, work and internal energy.

units.title: The Laws, Cycles and Engines
units.summary: The first law says you cannot win and the second says you cannot break even; an engine's efficiency is the price of that second sentence.
objectives: Apply the first law to a process and the second law to a direction.
Compute thermal efficiency for a cycle and compare it with the Carnot limit.

lessons.title: The First Law
lessons.objective: Apply the first law to a single process and to a complete cycle, and show why internal energy returns to its starting value.

lessons.title: The Second Law and Entropy
lessons.objective: State the second law in terms of both heat flow and entropy, and decide whether a proposed process can happen on its own.

lessons.title: Heat Engines and Thermodynamic Cycles
lessons.objective: Trace a working fluid around an Otto or Brayton cycle and mark where heat enters, work is done and heat is rejected.

lessons.title: Carnot Efficiency and the Third Law
lessons.objective: Compute Carnot efficiency from reservoir temperatures and explain why no cycle beats it and why absolute zero cannot be reached.

units.title: Heat Transfer
units.summary: Three modes with three different dependences on temperature, and deciding which one dominates is most of what a heat-transfer question is really asking.
objectives: Compute a conduction rate from conductivity, area, thickness and temperature difference.
Identify which mode dominates in a given situation and what slows it.

lessons.title: Conduction and Thermal Conductivity
lessons.objective: Use Fourier's law to compute a conduction rate and rank common materials by thermal conductivity.

lessons.title: Convection and Newton's Law of Cooling
lessons.objective: Distinguish natural from forced convection and use Newton's law of cooling to predict how a warm object approaches room temperature.

lessons.title: Emissivity, Absorptance and Kirchhoff's Law
lessons.objective: Explain why a good absorber is a good emitter, and read emissivity, absorptance and albedo from a description of a surface.

units.title: Radiation
units.summary: Everything above absolute zero radiates, and the fourth-power law is the reason a lamp filament can heat water from across a bench.
objectives: Relate a body's temperature to the spectrum it emits and to the total power it emits.
Compute the irradiance a surface receives from a source at a given distance.

lessons.title: Black-Body Radiation and Planck's Law
lessons.objective: Describe how an emitted spectrum shifts with temperature and use Wien's displacement law to find its peak wavelength.

lessons.title: Stefan-Boltzmann and Radiant Exitance
lessons.objective: Compute the radiant exitance of a surface from its temperature, emissivity and area, and show what doubling the temperature does.

lessons.title: Irradiance, Lamps and the Inverse-Square Law
lessons.objective: Compute the irradiance a surface receives from a lamp at a given distance and describe what an incandescent filament actually radiates.

units.title: The Radiant Collector
units.summary: The build is an energy balance with two terms: what the aperture lets in and what the walls let out. Every design choice moves one of them.
objectives: Choose surfaces, glazing and an aperture that raise the radiant power a collector absorbs.
Rank the conduction, convection and radiation losses from a warm enclosure and slow each one.

lessons.title: Absorbing Surfaces, Colour and Aperture
lessons.objective: Explain how surface colour, a selective coating, glazing and aperture size change the radiant power a collector absorbs.

lessons.title: Insulating Against All Three Modes
lessons.objective: Match an insulation strategy to the loss it slows, and compare materials by R-value and by emissivity.

lessons.title: Predicting the Temperature of Heated Water
lessons.objective: Estimate the final temperature of a known mass of water from absorbed radiant power, heating time and specific heat, then correct the estimate for losses.

units.title: How the Field Was Built
units.summary: Thermodynamics was assembled by people trying to fix steam engines and explain melting ice, and the event asks which of them did which.
objectives: Attribute latent heat, the ideal cycle and the mechanical equivalent of heat to the right people.
Say what entropy, kinetic theory and the quantum each replaced.

lessons.title: Black, Carnot and Joule
lessons.objective: Say what caloric theory got right, and attribute latent heat, the ideal cycle and the mechanical equivalent of heat correctly.

lessons.title: Kelvin, Clausius, Boltzmann, Maxwell and Planck
lessons.objective: Attribute the absolute scale, entropy, its statistical account, the distribution of molecular speeds and the quantum of radiation to the right figure.
